title: Role of Acute Phase Proteins In Diagnosis of Immune Thrombocytopenia
off: Role of Acute Phase Proteins In Diagnosis of Immune Thrombocytopenia
summary: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) are antibody-mediated disorders in which platelets are destroyed mainly through activating immunoglobulin (IgG) Fc receptors on phagocytes in the spleen and liver, eventually resulting in thrombocytopenia Acute phase proteins (APP) are inflammation markers that exhibit significant changes in serum concentration during inflammation. These are also important mediators produced in the liver during acute and chronic inflammatory states. Acute phase reactants can be classified as positive or negative, depending on their serum concentrations during inflammation. Positive acute phase reactants are upregulated, and their concentrations increase during inflammation. Negative acute phase reactants are downregulated, and their concentrations decrease during inflammation. Positive acute phase proteins include procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, ferritin, fibrinogen, hepcidin, and serum amyloid A. Negative acute phase reactants include albumin, prealbumin, transferrin, retinol-binding protein, and antithrombin CRP is now well established as a major acute phase protein and is used in daily clinical practice as a sensitive biomarker for infection and inflammation, with its level increasing from \<0.05 to \>500 mg/L after acute infections. CRP is produced by hepatocytes, in response to inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-1, with serum concentrations rising to \>5 mg/L after 6 hours and peaking after ∼48 hours. In healthy young adult volunteer blood donors, the median concentration of CRP was found to be ∼0.8 mg/L CRP levels are useful as a clinical diagnostic tool for infection, and it is a common knowledge that ITP is triggered by viral infection that precedes the clinical picture of ITP by a few days to a few weeks Procalcitonin (PCT) is used as a reliable inflammatory biomarker with high sensitivity and specificity ferritin was confirmed as an inflammation and infection biomarker in the diagnosis of viral and bacterial infections.

Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with platelet less than 100 × 109/L diagnosed as immune thrombocytopenia by bone marrow findings .

Age of patients : from 1 year to 50 years.

Exclusion Criteria:

* \- Other causes of thrombocytopenia as:

  * Hypersplenism.
  * Bone marrow diseases including : aplastic anemia, leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.
  * Cancer treatments like chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
  * Exposure to toxic chemicals as arsenic and benzene.
  * Medications to treat bacterial infections (antibiotics)and treat seizures or blood thinner heparin.

x.titre: Protéines de la phase aiguë dans le diagnostic du purpura thrombopénique immunologique
x.question: Le dosage de protéines de la phase aiguë (CRP, procalcitonine, ferritine) aide-t-il à diagnostiquer et classer le PTI, aigu ou chronique ?
x.contexte:
Le purpura thrombopénique immunologique (PTI) est une maladie à médiation par des anticorps : les plaquettes sont détruites principalement dans la rate et le foie après activation des récepteurs Fc des phagocytes. Le diagnostic reste un diagnostic d'exclusion, fondé sur la thrombopénie isolée et l'élimination des autres causes, avec parfois un myélogramme.

Le PTI est souvent déclenché par une infection virale survenant quelques jours à quelques semaines avant les symptômes. Les protéines de la phase aiguë sont des marqueurs d'inflammation produits par le foie. La CRP, la procalcitonine, la ferritine et le fibrinogène augmentent, tandis que l'albumine et la transferrine diminuent. Cette étude de l'Université de Sohag (Égypte) cherche à savoir si ces marqueurs diffèrent entre PTI aigu, PTI chronique et thrombopénies d'autres causes. Elle inclut 100 patients de 1 à 50 ans, avec thrombopénie < 100 G/L et PTI confirmé par la moelle osseuse. Les prélèvements servent à doser ces marqueurs.
x.interet: Les résultats pourraient dégager des marqueurs biologiques simples pour distinguer le PTI d'autres thrombopénies. L'étude est monocentrique et limitée à une population égyptienne.
x.profil: Des enfants et adultes de 1 à 50 ans avec thrombopénie et PTI confirmé, et des patients thrombopéniques d'autres causes.
